application_review: PROGRESS. The preceding recursive-localization round was rechecked before edits. Retained proof source hashes and axiom sets remain unchanged.

The abstract threshold theorem assumes a nonnegative size and convergence to zero of the correlation for every pair of selected sequences whose sizes vanish. Failure at every reciprocal positive threshold gives ultrafilter-large bad-parameter sets.

The verified slow-stage selection theorem chooses a reciprocal threshold tending to zero while retaining the bad-set property eventually. Witnesses are selected at each stage; nonempty parameter types supply arbitrary fallback witnesses. Squeezing their nonnegative sizes gives convergence to zero, contradicting the assumed null testing.
The tail-containing-ultrafilter hypothesis is explicit. No countable intersection of ultrafilter-large sets, bounded parameter cardinality, or extra compactness axiom is assumed.

For Gowers testing, admissible test functions are encoded as dependent unit-bounded subtypes. Their actual weighted Haar representatives have uniform L2 bounds. Vanishing weighted Gowers value makes their Hilbert image orthogonal to the actual dual space, and selected structured families consequently have zero limiting pairing.

The threshold is positive and uniform over every parameter and every unit test eventually along the same ultrafilter. It may depend on the fixed family, subgroup system, degree, weights and ultrafilter; it is not claimed to be a universal finitary Bessel modulus.

Finite products use the previously verified actual unit structured-product theorem. This establishes the testing threshold for paired coefficient products without discarding the original weights or assuming the parameters have bounded size.

The recursive-coefficient corollary uses an explicitly stated lower-intersection containment, which is the required input from a future concatenation induction hypothesis. Its threshold does not prove or assume that containment implicitly.

Four theorems are audited. Uniform Gowers testing thresholds for the fixed structured families are now proved. Full higher-order concatenation, qualitative Bessel and the original main target remain unproved.

A dependent-selection argument gives uniform small correlation from vanishing correlation for every selected parameter family, without bounded cardinality assumptions. Orthogonality to the lower intersection therefore controls all these recursive coefficients uniformly along the ultrafilter. A tail-containing ultrafilter now supplies a positive uniform testing threshold from null testing of every dependent selected sequence, proved by slow-stage diagonalization. Every selected actual unit family in a positive-degree dual space therefore admits one eventual Gowers threshold controlling all parameters and all unit tests.
